_comment: Canonical provenance records for the worked research claims. A status is deliberately multidimensional: sourceCheck says whether the cited material was inspected; reproduction describes computation; agreement records method dependence or dispute; interpretation prevents an editorial reading from masquerading as a computed fact; aiInvolvement records whether AI originated authoritative content (which is prohibited).

derivation.method: Count the root field across every Leeds v0.4 morphology token and sort descending.

limitations: The figures inherit the Leeds corpus's root assignments and tokenization.
Frequency does not establish the meaning or importance of a root in context.
The primary registry record does not assert an independently verified modern edition or page locator.
The claim concerns the documented lineage of a reading method, not the correctness of that method.

derivation.method: Count tokens whose Leeds root field is ywm; the resulting root total is the only numerical total this record reproduces.

limitations: The total changes when the unit is changed from annotated roots to selected surface or compound forms.
Widely circulated 365 and 475 totals have not been reproduced here and lack an inspected source in this evidence record.

derivation.method: Count distinct verses in which both Leeds root fields occur.

limitations: The result inherits the Leeds corpus's root assignments.
Verse-level co-occurrence does not by itself establish a semantic relationship.

derivation.method: Count normalized surface forms and root fields with exactly one occurrence.

limitations: Hapax totals depend on the corpus's tokenization and normalization.
A surface-form hapax and a root hapax are different units.

derivation.method: Group Leeds root occurrences by the Cairo 1924 Meccan/Medinan surah classification.

limitations: The boundary totals can change under another chronology classification.
The result inherits the Leeds corpus's root assignments.

derivation.method: Compare root-field totals with a selected-surface-form parity claim.

limitations: The asserted parity depends on selecting particular surface forms.
The root a-kh-r also carries senses other than ‘the hereafter’.

derivation.method: Count every morphology token, every verse row, and every distinct root value across the bundled Leeds v0.4 files.

limitations: Token and verse totals follow the Leeds corpus's tokenization and the Kufan verse division it encodes; other counting rules give different totals.
The 1,642 distinct roots figure counts root spellings as the corpus records them, including a small number of contested assignments.

derivation.method: For every token, test whether the Leeds morphology assigns a triliteral root; report the with-root share and the part-of-speech distribution of the remainder.

limitations: The 64.53% share is a property of Arabic grammar plus the corpus's annotation choices, not a data gap: most rootless tokens are particles, pronouns, and other function words that have no root by definition.
Any root-based statistic on this site describes the 49,967 rooted tokens, not all 77,429.
